questions.question_text: A shell is fired from level ground at $60\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, with $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$. What is its greatest height?

options.why: Used $60\cos 30^{\circ}$ as the initial vertical velocity instead of $60\sin 30^{\circ}$.
Left out the $-5t^{2}$ term, computing only $\dot{y}(0) \times t$.
Used $60\cos 30^{\circ}$ for the vertical velocity and also left out the $-5t^{2}$ term.

questions.solution_text:
$\dot{y} = -10t + 60\sin 30^{\circ}$
$= -10t + 30$
1. **Find the time at which the feature occurs**
$0 = -10t + 30$
$t = 3$
2. **Substitute that time into the required equation of motion**
$y(3) = -5(3)^{2} + 30(3)$
$= -45 + 90$
$= 45\text{ m}$

questions.question_text: A ball is projected from level ground at $35\text{ m/s}$ at an angle $\theta$ with $\sin\theta = 0.6$ and $\cos\theta = 0.8$. Taking $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$, what is the time of flight?

options.why: Used the horizontal component $35 \times 0.8 = 28$ as the initial vertical velocity.
Stopped at the time to reach the greatest height instead of the whole flight.
Used the horizontal component as the vertical velocity and stopped at the greatest height.

questions.question_text: A ball is hit from level ground at $24\text{ m/s}$ at $60^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, with $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$. What is its range, to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Substituted the time to the greatest height instead of the full time of flight.
Multiplied the time of flight by the vertical component $24\sin 60^{\circ}$ instead of the horizontal component.
Used the vertical component and the time to the greatest height.

questions.solution_text:
$\dot{x} = 24\cos 60^{\circ} = 12$
$\dot{y}(0) = 24\sin 60^{\circ} = 12\sqrt{3}$
1. **Find the time at which the feature occurs**
$0 = -5t^{2} + 12\sqrt{3}\,t$
$t = \dfrac{12\sqrt{3}}{5} = 4.1569\ldots$
2. **Substitute that time into the required equation of motion**
$x = 12(4.1569\ldots)$
$= 49.9\text{ m}$

questions.question_text: A ball is rolled horizontally at $18\text{ m/s}$ off a cliff $125\text{ m}$ high. Taking the launch point as the origin and $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$, how long does it take to reach the ground?

options.why: Wrote the vertical displacement as $-10t^{2}$, forgetting the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in $\frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$.
Solved $t^{2} = 25$ but never took the square root.
Used $-10t^{2}$ and also failed to take the square root.

questions.solution_text:
$\dot{y}(0) = 0$, so $y = -5t^{2}$
$-125 = -5t^{2}$
$t^{2} = 25$
$t = 5$ (as $t \ge 0$)
The ball reaches the ground after $5$ seconds.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched from the origin at $50\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, with $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$. What is its speed after $4$ seconds, to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Swapped sine and cosine, taking $\dot{x} = 50\sin 30^{\circ}$ and $\dot{y}(0) = 50\cos 30^{\circ}$.
Added the two components instead of using $\sqrt{\dot{x}^{2} + \dot{y}^{2}}$.
Swapped sine and cosine and then added the components instead of using Pythagoras.

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown from the top of a $40\text{ m}$ tower at $30\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ above the horizontal. Taking the launch point as the origin and $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$, what is its speed when it hits the ground, to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Assumed the path is symmetric, so the landing speed equals the launch speed; that holds only when the landing level equals the launch level.
Used only the vertical velocity at landing and ignored the horizontal component.
Used the symmetric landing time $t = 3$ and then took only the vertical velocity.

questions.solution_text:
$\dot{x} = 15\sqrt{3}$, $\dot{y} = -10t + 15$, $y = -5t^{2} + 15t$
1. **Find the time at which the feature occurs**
$-40 = -5t^{2} + 15t$
$t^{2} - 3t - 8 = 0$
$t = \dfrac{3 + \sqrt{41}}{2} = 4.7015\ldots$ (as $t \ge 0$)
2. **Substitute that time into the required equation of motion**
$\dot{y} = -10(4.7015\ldots) + 15 = -32.0156\ldots$
Speed $= \sqrt{\left(15\sqrt{3}\right)^{2} + (-32.0156\ldots)^{2}}$
$= \sqrt{675 + 1025.0\ldots}$
$= 41.2\text{ m/s}$

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown from the top of a $140\text{ m}$ cliff at $30\text{ m/s}$ at $30^{\circ}$ **below** the horizontal. Taking the launch point as the origin and $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$, how long does it take to reach the ground?

options.why: Took the initial vertical velocity as $+15$, using the symmetry of the path even though the launch and landing levels differ.
Ignored the initial vertical velocity, solving $-5t^{2}=-140$ as though the stone were thrown horizontally.
Divided the $140\text{ m}$ drop by the $15\text{ m/s}$ downward component, treating the fall as though that speed stayed constant.

questions.solution_text:
$\dot{y}=-10t-30\sin 30^{\circ}=-10t-15$
$y=-5t^{2}-15t$
The ground is $140\text{ m}$ below the launch point, so $y=-140$.
$-140=-5t^{2}-15t$
$5t^{2}+15t-140=0$
$t^{2}+3t-28=0$
$(t+7)(t-4)=0$
$t=-7$ or $t=4$
The root $t=-7$ is rejected because $t\ge 0$.
The stone reaches the ground after $4$ seconds.

questions.question_text: A ball is thrown from level ground at $40\text{ m/s}$ at $45^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, with $g=10\text{ m/s}^{2}$. For how long is the ball more than $30\text{ m}$ above the ground, to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Gave the later time at which the ball is at $30\text{ m}$ rather than the length of the interval between the two times.
Gave the earlier time at which the ball reaches $30\text{ m}$ rather than the interval between the two times.
Added the two times instead of subtracting them.
